cells.tense: You are carrying what has to be carried right now, in a way that can flex.
cells.act: sit with someone in it without fixing it
cells.ask: Next time someone close to you is struggling, sit with them a few minutes and don't fix it — no advice, no tidying. Keep your own sense of things while you do.
cells.core:
There's a weight on you at the moment and you're carrying it without hardening around it. When something hurts and you stay soft enough to keep adjusting, that isn't weakness leaking through — that's the thing working. You can feel where the pressure is and you're not pretending it away.

So let some of it be shared. Next time someone close to you is struggling, sit with them a few minutes and don't fix it — no advice, no tidying them up. Keep your own sense of things while you do. You'll find you can hold their weight and yours at once without either going flat, and that nobody has to be absorbed into the other for it to count.
cells.sheetLine: You can carry this and still bend.
cells.verb: bearing what's in front of you without going rigid
cells.place: at the point where you keep adjusting, moment to moment

cells.tense: You are bracing against what might come next, holding harder than the moment requires.
cells.act: adjust the share until it is fair, then stop
cells.ask: Where a load is carried alongside someone else, shift the share until it's genuinely even, then stop — say out loud you've stopped, and leave their half with them.
cells.core:
You're holding things so far ahead that your grip has stopped being about now. What used to bend has stiffened into something braced. You're set for a strain that hasn't arrived, and that bracing is costing you the ease you'd need to meet the one that does. Around you, people feel the over-tightness without being able to name it.

What's thin here isn't effort, it's proportion. Where a load is carried alongside someone else, shift the share until it's genuinely even, then stop — say out loud you've stopped, and leave their half with them. You don't have to keep compensating in advance; you can find the fair point, put it down, and the ground under you is steadier for it, not less.
cells.sheetLine: You're holding so hard the shape has stopped being true.
cells.verb: bearing what's in front of you without going rigid

cells.tense: Under pressure you folded, and you have not come back out to where the pressure is.
cells.act: put it down and leave your hands empty a while
cells.ask: Choose something you've been clutching and set it down for a few days — not lost, just placed where you can see it. Wait with your hands free and notice what's there.
cells.core:
There was a load you couldn't carry, and something in you learned that holding is where it breaks. Since then you've stayed clear of the places where weight gets put on you, and from the outside it looks like calm. Inside, you're stationed at a door you've already walked through, checking whether it's safe to come back.

Setting something down is what brings you back. Choose something you've been clutching and set it down for a few days — not lost, just placed where you can see it. Wait with your hands free and notice what's there. You'll find that letting go on your own terms doesn't feel like the floor giving way, and the next weight arrives at a strength that was already yours.
cells.sheetLine: You're guarding a threshold you already crossed.
cells.verb: bearing what's in front of you without going rigid
cells.place: at the point where you keep adjusting, moment to moment

cells.tense: You are bearing what you bear without seeing that the strength is yours.
cells.act: move toward the thing you actually want
cells.ask: Name something you'd like, small and only yours, and take one step toward it this week — before calling it sensible. Then notice who moved.
cells.core:
There's strength in how you hold things, and also a version where you keep collapsing under what others seem to manage — and you don't count yourself as either. The hands doing the work don't get named. You talk about getting through as if it happened to you rather than being the way you operate.

Wanting is the way back in. Name something you'd like, small and only yours, and take one step toward it this week — before calling it sensible, before checking it against anyone's needs. Then notice who moved. You'll find the desire and the loading come from the same place, and that seeing where you're going tells you whose strength has been under it the whole time.
cells.sheetLine: The strength in your hands is yours and goes unnamed.
cells.verb: bearing what's in front of you without going rigid
cells.place: at the point where you keep adjusting, moment to moment

attempts.check: Unsupported claim: that the person is holding something specific under pressure at all — the record gives a capacity, not their history, so every cell locates the mechanism and leaves the content to them. Reader's likely objection: 'I'm not gripping anything, I just keep my life upright' — so Too Much ends on contact under load and asks it of the next stretch, not the past. The asks survive being wrong because each is a small act anyone can try and learn from whether or not the read lands. Sentence that serves the writer more than them: 'capacity that contains rather than crushes' — cut; it praises the card, not the person.
